dynamic_headline: Fed/rates leads a constructive but selective pre-market setup.
market_summary: The pre-market setup is constructive but selective, based on 1869 articles from Yahoo Finance, TradingView, simplywall.st, MarketBeat, The Motley Fool. The dominant theme is macro, with 913 macro items, 517 company items, 398 industry items, and 41 policy items. The tape looks more useful for identifying near-term rotation and risk appetite than for making a single directional index call.

market_narrative.headline: Fed/rates keeps risk appetite constructive but selective as investors await confirmation
market_narrative.summary: US equities are carrying a constructive but selective bias as Fed/rates, inflation, oil/energy shape positioning. Investors are balancing selective leadership against the risk that policy, rates or growth data broadens the pressure.

key_forces.label: Negative driver
key_forces.text: Headline and policy uncertainty keep the risk premium elevated

key_forces.label: Main theme
key_forces.text: Positioning is waiting for confirmation from futures, Treasury yields and opening breadth

watch_next: futures, Treasury yields and opening breadth

index_performance_summary: Nasdaq and growth indexes should be the most sensitive part of the tape when AI, semiconductor, mega-cap tech, or guidance stories dominate. S&P 500 direction is likely to remain tied to Treasury yields, Fed expectations, inflation data, and broad risk appetite. Dow and equal-weight exposure may react more to policy, regulation, tariff, and industrial-cycle headlines.
macro_outlook: Macro coverage is concentrated around Fed/rates (326), inflation (203), oil/energy (119), growth/jobs (31). The practical implication is that equity rallies may need confirmation from rates and inflation expectations; if yields rise while growth headlines weaken, risk appetite can fade quickly.
risk_and_sentiment: Sentiment is constructive but selective: 250 positive, 202 negative, and 1417 neutral articles. My read is to avoid treating headline volume as conviction by itself; the more important signal is whether macro-sensitive and technology-sensitive stories are pointing in the same direction.

themes.title: Fed Policy & Rate Path
themes.current_view: Fed policy is still restrictive, but investors are watching whether softer data pulls rate-cut expectations forward.
themes.what_changed: The rate path is becoming the main valuation channel for long-duration equity exposure.
themes.why_it_matters: Rate cuts support multiples, but cuts driven by weaker growth can also pressure earnings expectations.

market_impact.equities: Neutral for indexes, supportive for duration if growth holds.
sectors: Negative: Banks if yield curves flatten

themes.title: Growth & Labor Market
themes.current_view: Growth risk is the key constraint on equity upside.
themes.what_changed: Investors need to separate healthy cooling from recession risk.
themes.why_it_matters: Labor and demand data affect both forward earnings and the policy reaction function.

themes.title: AI & Technology Leadership
themes.current_view: AI leadership remains the strongest equity-specific macro channel.
themes.what_changed: Mega-cap technology and semiconductor narratives continue to carry index leadership.
themes.why_it_matters: Concentrated leadership can support indexes while also raising valuation and crowding risk.

market_impact.equities: Supportive for Nasdaq if yields remain contained.

themes.title: Earnings & Valuation
themes.current_view: The equity market needs earnings delivery to justify elevated multiples.
themes.what_changed: Macro sensitivity is shifting from inflation-only toward margins, guidance and demand durability.
themes.why_it_matters: Valuation leaves less room for disappointment when growth signals weaken.

market_impact.rates: Lower yields can help multiples but not earnings.

equities.reason: Policy support is partly offset by growth and earnings uncertainty.

rates.reason: Softer data would support lower yields, but inflation surprises remain a risk.

growth_stocks.reason: Duration exposure benefits from lower yields, while valuation leaves limited margin for error.

financials.reason: Lower yields can pressure net interest margins while a softer economy raises credit sensitivity.
